html:
In September 2025 young people in Nepal, calling themselves Gen Z, rose against a ban on social media and against corruption, and brought down the government of Prime Minister K. P. Sharma Oli within two days.

The protests began in Kathmandu on 8 September. Police opened fire and killed many young protesters, and the anger turned to fury. The next day crowds set fire to the parliament building, party offices and politicians' homes, and Oli resigned. Many more died before the army restored order.

Organisers used the chat app Discord to choose an interim leader, the former chief justice Sushila Karki, who became Nepal's first woman prime minister and promised new elections. The rising echoed the July uprising in Bangladesh and the Aragalaya in Sri Lanka, and it was the third time since the 1990 movement that street protest had changed Nepal's rulers.
sum: In September 2025 young people in Nepal, calling themselves Gen Z, rose against a ban on social media and against corruption, and brought down the government of Prime Minister K. P. Sharma Oli within two days.
